hrl_001: You can recognise it by its low, wide shape, branching almost from the ground, with flower candles starting at head height in May. It stands on the west side of the Hoofdweg, Nieuw-Vennep.
hrl_003: You can recognise it in winter by its matt black, hoof-shaped buds, nothing else here has them. It stands on the Hoofdweg, Nieuw-Vennep, a few doors from the older chestnut.
hrl_004: You can recognise it in April by sharp yellow-green flowers opening before the leaves, and milky white sap in a broken twig. It stands at the Hervormde church, Nieuw-Vennep.
hrl_006: You can recognise it in midsummer by strings of winged nutlets hanging half a metre long from every branch tip. It stands on the Markt, in front of the market hall, Hoofddorp.
hrl_007: You can recognise it by its dense, rounded crown reaching down to head height, standing in an ordinary planting strip. It stands on the Spieringweg, opposite the Fortwachter, Vijfhuizen.
hrl_008: You can recognise it by its bark flaking away in a camouflage pattern of grey, green and cream. It stands in front of a notary's office at Hoofdweg 669, corner of Manegelaan.
hrl_009: You can recognise it by its falling branches forming a tent shape, hemmed onto a traffic island rather than open parkland. It stands where the Hoofdweg meets the ring road, Hoofddorp.
hrl_010: You can recognise it by its full, healthy crown, visible the whole way along the road from a private front garden. It stands at Nieuwemeerdijk 143, Badhoevedorp.
